text:
nina: Quick heads-up — I opened a small migration PR for the Optimize Toolkit docs about token-bundling behavior when switching quantization profiles. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4873. Need docs + runtime eyes.

jordan: Nice. Can you add a concise Python SDK example showing how to enable batching + kv prefetch in the new surface? e.g. `client.optimize.request(..., batching='auto', kv_prefetch=True, quant_profile='econ-8')`

eli: Prefer `batching='auto'` indeed. Also call out the default `max_tokens_per_batch` change in the migration note — that bit caused confusion in staging. I can add a short code block for Go.

nina: I'll add both Python and Go snippets. @eli @sam can you sanity-check runtime behaviour for `econ-8` + kv-prefetch on dedicated?

sam: Did a quick dedicated smoke: econ-8 + kv_prefetch -> ~12% throughput improvement for short seqs, small regression on long-context perplexity. Logged perf note in the PR and attached microbench logs.

pr-reviewer: Heads-up: the migration guide currently links to `/docs/kv-cache` (old). I'll update the link to `/docs/caching/kv` in a follow-up commit.

docs-bot: Reminder — PR needs frontmatter YML (sidebar: opt-toolkit, tags: [migration, snippets]) and TOC entry. Also include a short changelog bullet.

nina: Adding a short canary rollout recommendation: start 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with telemetry checks at each step. Will include sample query set and expected `batch_size_percentile` targets.

jordan: Please cross-link to the telemetry note: https://redwood.ai/telemetry/batching and mention how to read `batch_latency_p95` vs `batch_latency_median`.

eli: I'll review the PR tonight and add the Go snippet with `kv_prefetch_enabled` naming to match SDK conventions. If no blockers I'll greenlight merge tomorrow AM and coordinate the runtime flag flip.

sam: LGTM on the rollout numbers. small nit: use `kv_prefetch_enabled` in examples (Go) and `kv_prefetch` in Python to reflect current bindings.

nina: Thanks — pushing updates in a few mins. :thumbsup:

jordan: tiny doc nit after merge: add a one-liner about cost delta when enabling kv-prefetch for high QPS workloads.

eli: noted, will add cost guidance and a short equation to estimate extra token-store reads per minute.

nina: Closing loop — once merged I'll open a follow-up to add an automated sample test in the examples repo that runs the sample prompts against both profiles for regression checks.
